# opencode-shell

Run local Bash commands from the OpenCode prompt with `!!`, without sending them to the model:

```text
!! pwd
!! git status
```

Commands run in the active session's directory (or the current project on the home screen). Recent output and exit status appear beneath the home prompt or above the session composer. A single `!` still uses OpenCode's native shell mode. Modified Enter keys still insert newlines.

## Requirements

Version **0.3.0** supports **OpenCode `>=2.0.25 <3`** and uses `@opencode/plugin`'s V2 server and CLI APIs. OpenCode 1.x users should keep `opencode-shell@0.2.0`.

## Install from npm

Add the package to the plural `plugins` array in **`~/.config/opencode/cli.json`**, preserving other entries:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json",
  "plugins": ["opencode-shell@0.3.0"]
}
```

This CLI-only configuration keeps the plugin local even when connected to a remote server. The package also has an inert server entrypoint, so loading it through `plugins` in `opencode.jsonc` automatically exposes its CLI component. Do not configure both copies. Quit and restart OpenCode after changing the loading configuration.

V2 uses `cli.json`, not V1's `tui.json`. See the [CLI plugin guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/cli).

## Install from source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/edwardEsmerson/opencode-shell.git ~/src/opencode-plugins/opencode-shell
cd ~/src/opencode-plugins/opencode-shell
npm ci
```

Use the absolute checkout directory in `cli.json`:

```json
{
  "plugins": ["/home/you/src/opencode-plugins/opencode-shell"]
}
```

Root `index.ts` and `tui.ts` and npm package exports all forward to precompiled `dist/` JavaScript. OpenTUI's runtime Solid transform skips `node_modules`, so publishing raw TSX loses reactive rendering. `npm run build` applies Solid's universal renderer transform without bundling OpenTUI or Solid; the host shares those runtime imports. `npm ci`, packing, and publishing build automatically through `prepare`.

Use either the checkout or the npm package, not both. After source changes, run `npm run build` and restart OpenCode.

## Behavior and development

`src/tui.tsx` registers V2 slots and scopes interception to the prompt editor found beside its footer contribution. It uses the exposed OpenTUI renderer because V2 no longer exposes V1 prompt refs. The nearby render-tree lookup is tested against OpenCode 2.0.25; it fails closed when no prompt is found and does not intercept dialog textareas. `!!` is consumed and cleared before submission, including an empty prefix. Active commands are aborted and listeners/slots removed on plugin cleanup.

`src/shell.ts` parses commands and runs Bash. Shell runs are local to the CLI, including with a remote server; remote-only paths are not translated. `src/index.ts` and the retained `/server` subpath register no server hooks or model-callable tools.

```sh
npm ci
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm pack --dry-run
```

OpenTUI declares Node `>=26.4.0` or Bun `>=1.3.0`; prefer a supported runtime for development. Tests cover package and local host resolution, interception, native shell passthrough, multiline editing, working directories, subprocess cancellation, and compiled output updating without a remount. The rendering regression uses Solid's real universal runtime with an in-memory backend; live OpenCode checks cover native rendering. The development lockfile overrides Seroval to a patched release; npm overrides do not change a consumer's host dependencies.

Before release, smoke-test both home and session prompts in a fresh OpenCode instance: `!! pwd`, single-`!` native mode, empty `!!`, multiline input, unrelated dialogs, and plugin cleanup during a running command. `prepublishOnly` runs typechecking and all tests.
